{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOU4GkE88AAAABi_MlUQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlaE0zhMVYB4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlaE0", "number": 66, "title": "Use utterance-aware audio segmentation for AI Livestream speech recognition", "body": "## Problem

After #62 / PR #63, the owner reports that the lighter local model now produces comments on Pixel 7a, whereas previously none appeared. However, comments remain too infrequent and speech recognition can receive incomplete utterances. The current `projects/ai-livestream/audio-worklet.js` collects fixed 96,000-sample (6-second at 16 kHz) non-overlapping windows and uses a simple RMS/voiced-sample threshold before submission. It can split sentences at arbitrary boundaries or wait unnecessarily after someone finishes speaking. `MIN_AUDIO_INTERVAL` (5.5 s), `MIN_COMMENT_INTERVAL` (8 s), and the bounded worker/pending-window logic also constrain delivery.

## Goal

Replace the rigid fixed-window capture strategy with lightweight **utterance-aware voice activity detection (VAD) / endpointing**, so recognition begins shortly after a natural pause or end of speech, preserving coherent speech segments where practical. Improve perceived responsiveness and transcription input quality without creating excessive CPU/GPU load on a Pixel 7a-class phone. Keep all media and inference in the browser.

## Scope

- Investigate suitable low-cost VAD/endpointing approaches and choose the implementation and thresholds based on evidence. A short trailing-silence threshold (e.g. 0.5–0.8 s) is a starting hypothesis, not a fixed requirement. Prefer simple lightweight processing over a new heavyweight model.
- Detect speech onset and end, include bounded pre-roll/tail where useful to avoid clipping syllables, and submit a completed voiced segment promptly after the endpoint rather than waiting for an arbitrary six-second boundary. Preserve the required 16 kHz mono PCM format.
- Handle very short utterances, normal brief pauses within sentences, sustained speech without a pause, quiet speech, background noise, and silence. Use a bounded maximum segment duration and an appropriate split strategy for continuous speech, with no unbounded recording or queue.
- Adapt the worker's audio length validation and any capture-specific throttling/backpressure to the new variable-length segments. Ensure an old fixed-window interval does not unnecessarily delay a completed utterance. Keep one active job and a bounded pending policy; avoid parallel ASR calls, unbounded catch-up bursts, indefinite starvation, and excessive invocations for rapid pauses.
- Preserve session cancellation, microphone/camera release, language switching, privacy, local-only inference, and responsive UI. Keep the current Whisper Base recognizer, task-trained 0.6B comment model, baseline route, audience simulation, and current relaxed comment-quality policy. Do not add semantic comment filters, retrain models, or redesign the UI. Changes to comment cadence/batching beyond what is necessary for the audio segmentation integration are a separate experiment.

## Verification

- Add deterministic synthetic PCM / timing fixtures that exercise speech followed by a pause, internal brief pauses, multiple utterances, long continuous speech, silence/noise, onset/tail preservation, maximum buffer bounds, slow ASR, cancellation and pending-window handling. Verify that valid short segments can reach recognition before the old six-second deadline.
- Compare the old fixed-window behavior against the new segmentation using representative scripted speech/pause patterns. Report segment boundaries, recognition submission delay, ASR invocation count, audio duration processed, and available CPU/latency or resource measurements. If useful, use existing Japanese/English audio fixtures to illustrate recognition differences. Do not claim improved transcription accuracy or actual mobile performance without evidence.
- Run applicable automated unit/browser regression tests and the normal repository build/CI. Prefer focused tests and reuse existing validation; no extensive model-quality reevaluation or mandatory heavyweight benchmark merely for this change.

## Acceptance criteria

1. In supported browsers, completed speech is submitted promptly following an appropriate pause rather than only at fixed six-second boundaries; continuous speech still produces bounded recognition opportunities.
2. Automated fixtures demonstrate correct segmentation, bounded buffers/work, silence handling, timely submission, and lifecycle/backpressure behavior without new material functional or performance regressions.
3. The implementation records the chosen endpointing strategy, tradeoffs and reproducible comparison with fixed-window capture. No guaranteed improvement in subjective transcription/comment quality or arbitrary numerical speedup is required.
4. Existing local inference, privacy and model selection behavior remains intact; applicable automated checks pass.

**The owner will test the merged demo personally on Pixel 7a and Mac. Physical-device testing, human evaluation, perfect ASR accuracy, and comment quality are NOT review, merge, or Issue closure gates.** This is a bounded incremental experiment. Once the implementation and applicable automated validation are complete, merge normally and verify deployment afterwards.
